title: Nuclear pharmacy permit, renewal, the qualified nuclear pharmacist, and the nuclear pharmacy's change duties
rule_summary: Under M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39B the Board may register an establishment for transacting business as a nuclear pharmacy; a nuclear pharmacy shall not perform any pharmacy functions other than the dispensing of radiopharmaceutical drug products; the Board may deny registration if in its discretion the pharmacy would be inconsistent with or opposed to the best interest of the public health, welfare and safety; no registration or permit shall be made or issued to a corporation unless management is in the hands of a registered pharmacist; the permit expires on December 31 of each uneven numbered year following issue; and the Board shall render a final decision within 150 days after the filing of an application, failure to do so, except when caused by the applicant's delay, constituting approval with the permit to be issued. 247 CMR 13.03(6) to (10) repeat these terms (the Board may require the applicant to appear; a corporation's nuclear pharmacy must be managed and operated by a registered pharmacist in good standing) and 13.03(3) to (5) condition issue on required publications, equipment and premises. Under 247 CMR 13.04 each permit expires on December 31st of each uneven numbered year following issuance, and renewal is made on a Board renewal form fully and properly completed and submitted in a timely manner with the required payment. Under 247 CMR 13.02 a qualified nuclear pharmacist is a pharmacist registered under M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24, employed in a nuclear pharmacy, who has submitted satisfactory evidence of meeting the education, training and experience requirements and has received from the Board an official letter finding the pharmacist qualified. Under 247 CMR 13.06 a qualified nuclear pharmacist shall be currently registered under s. 24; have 200 contact hours of formal academic training in radiopharmaceutical preparation and handling, no more than 60 of them through laboratory training; have in addition a minimum of three months full-time, or 500 hours, of actual on-the-job experience under the supervision of a qualified nuclear pharmacist in a nuclear pharmacy, or in a structured nuclear pharmacy training program of a Board-approved college or school of pharmacy; and submit a detailed affidavit of experience and training to the Board. Under 247 CMR 13.05 no person other than a qualified nuclear pharmacist shall be employed to direct and manage the pharmacy; only designated qualified nuclear pharmacists conduct its radiopharmaceutical activities, and at least one shall be in personal attendance at all times, and on the premises during the entire time the pharmacy is open for business; detailed records of acquisition and disposition of all radiopharmaceuticals are kept in readily retrievable form for at least three years and available to the Board or its agents for inspection on request; the permit and the certificate of personal registration of each full-time registered pharmacist are posted in a conspicuous place, and the name of the director of pharmacy services is displayed in letters not less than one inch high; in advance of any move the pharmacy submits an application for a new permit with fees, and it shall not operate at the new location until approved and issued a new permit and a new controlled substances registration; a nuclear pharmacy being established, remodeled or relocated first submits its structural plans for Board review and approval; and within ten days of the commencement or termination of employment of any pharmacist it reports that employment or termination to the Board.
exam_relevance: Tests the nuclear pharmacy's separate permit and its deemed-approval rule, the training numbers for a qualified nuclear pharmacist, and the ten-day staffing report.

exceptions: The deemed approval after 150 days does not apply where the failure to act is caused by the delay of the applicant.
common_confusions: A nuclear pharmacy may not perform pharmacy functions other than dispensing radiopharmaceutical drug products, so it does not operate as a retail pharmacy.
Registration as a pharmacist is not enough to direct a nuclear pharmacy: the Board's official letter finding the pharmacist qualified is part of the definition.
A nuclear pharmacy that has moved may not operate at the new site until it holds a new permit and a new controlled substances registration.
verification_notes: Read in the text of M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39B on malegislature.gov and in the Board's publication of 247 CMR 13.00 (PDF) on mass.gov on 2026-09-17. The publication contains two differently numbered versions of the later paragraphs of 247 CMR 13.05, so paragraphs from 13.05(14) onward are described here without paragraph numbers.
